items.followUp: What was Mendeleev’s contribution to the classification of elements?

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying him as a Russian chemist.

rubric.why: States how Mendeleev classified the elements.
rubric.description: He arranged the elements in a periodic table in order of increasing atomic masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing his periodic table and its arrangement by atomic masses.

modelAnswer: Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist.
He arranged the elements in a periodic table in order of increasing atomic masses.

items.followUp: Name the two series that make up the f-block of the periodic table.

rubric.why: Locates the f-block beneath the main body of the periodic table.
rubric.description: The f-block is shown in two separate rows at the bottom of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly locating the f-block below the main table.

rubric.why: Names both series that make up the f-block.
rubric.description: The two rows are the lanthanide and actinide series.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both series.

modelAnswer: The f-block is shown as two separate rows at the bottom of the periodic table.
These rows are the lanthanide and actinide series.

items.followUp: Identify the types of covalent bonds in N₂ and H₂.

rubric.why: Identifies the bond between the carbon atoms in C₂H₂ as a triple bond.
rubric.description: C₂H₂ has a triple covalent bond between its two carbon atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the C–C bond as triple.

rubric.why: Identifies the bonds between carbon and hydrogen in CH₄ as single bonds.
rubric.description: CH₄ has single covalent bonds between carbon and hydrogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the bonds in methane as single.

modelAnswer: C₂H₂: the two carbon atoms are joined by a triple covalent bond.
CH₄: carbon and hydrogen atoms are joined by single covalent bonds.
